svg.title: Tarjan's Single-Pass Strongly Connected Components (SCC) Algorithm
svg.desc: Animated step-by-step trace of Tarjan's SCC algorithm computing discovery[u] and low[u] on graph A->B->C->A, C->D, D->E->D, updating low via on-stack back edges, ignoring cross-component edges to off-stack nodes, and popping complete SCCs whenever low[u] == discovery[u].
svg.text: discovery[u], low[u], On-Stack Back-Edge Updates, and Root Extraction (low[u] === discovery[u]) in Theta(V + E)

g.text: Step 1: DFS enters A(1,1) -> B(2,2) -> C(3,3)
Each node initializes low[u] = discovery[u] and pushes onto the Tarjan stack.
From C, explore outgoing edge C -> D first (before back-edge C -> A).
Step 2: Traverse C -> D(4,4) -> E(5,5). Stack: [A, B, C, D, E]
At E, examine edge E -> D. Notice D is currently ON THE STACK!
Step 3: At D: low[D] == disc[D] == 4 -> ROOT! Pop SCC {E, D}
Popping down to D removes E and D from stack & marks D and E off-stack.
Backtrack to C: why doesn't C set low[C] = min(3, low[D])? Because D is OFF stack? Wait: D was tree child!
Step 4: C inspects back-edge C -> A (A is ON stack!)
low[C] = min(3, disc[A]=1) = 1! (Also min(3, low[D]=4) kept 3.)
Since low[C]=1 != disc[C]=3, C is NOT an SCC root -> stays on stack!
Step 5: Backtrack to B: low[B] = min(2, low[C]=1) = 1
low[B]=1 != disc[B]=2, so B stays on stack too. Unwind to A.
At A: low[A] = min(1, low[B]=1) = 1 === disc[A] -> ROOT OF SCC #2!
Step 6: Pop C, B, A -> SCC #2 = {A, B, C}! All SCCs Found!
Bonus: Tarjan outputs SCCs in REVERSE topological order of the condensation DAG!

svg.text: The 3 Core Rules of Tarjan's Algorithm:
1. Tree edge (v unvisited): dfs(v); low[u] = Math.min(low[u], low[v]);
2. Back edge (v on stack): low[u] = Math.min(low[u], discovery[v]);
3. Cross edge (v OFF stack): IGNORE! (v belongs to an already-popped SCC)
4. Root condition: if (low[u] === discovery[u]) pop stack down to u -> 1 SCC!
Critical bug guard: NEVER update low[u] from a cross-edge to an off-stack node v (if (onStack[v])), or disconnected SCCs collapse into one!
